item.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
item.description: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. item.title: ICLR 2027's new 1–4 scale: a 2, 2, 3 is better than it feels [P]
item.description: ICLR 2027 moved to a 4-point scale (1 clear reject, 2 weak reject, 3 weak accept, 4 clear accept), so nobody has a feel yet for what a given set of scores means. We counted the public scores on OpenReview: 73,410 reviews on 23,759 submissions. A couple of things that surprised us: [1] 57% of all reviews are a 2. Only 1.5% are a 4. [2] The median paper averages exactly 2.0. So a 2, 2, 3 (mean 2.33) is already above most papers. item.title: Don't Replace, Complement: A Detector-Agnostic Subspace Signal for Near-OOD Detection
item.description: Post-hoc out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is mature on far-OOD yet remains weak on near-OOD. These two settings differ in their use of class-characteristic feature directions: far-OOD inputs largely fail to activate those of their predicted class, whereas near-OOD inputs activate them much as in-distribution samples do. Because the axis separating far-OOD leaves near-OOD almost indistinguishable from ID, a score optimized for one setting is misaligned with the other; where a detector already saturates far-OOD, added near-OOD sensitivity is bought partly against it. item.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
item.description: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. item.title: Aligning Policy Encoders with a Shape Teacher
item.description: 3D-aware representations can improve robotic manipulation by providing geometric information that is robust to changes in viewpoint, object position, and occlusion. However, using 3D inputs at deployment requires additional sensing and processing, making image-based policies more practical. We ask whether an image-based policy can acquire 3D shape information during training while retaining a purely image-based interface at deployment.
